speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to help me understand the cause, have these symptoms been present since you woke up today, or did they develop gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: The progression of weakness over a few weeks, combined with your significant weight loss and history of anabolic steroid use, suggests a specific pathology; have you noticed any muscle atrophy (wasting) in your right arm compared to your left?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Brachial Plexopathy (specifically Pancoast tumor affecting the lower trunk).

Given your age, significant weight loss, history of heavy smoking, and the combination of progressive weakness, atrophy, and sensory changes in one arm, I need to confirm the presence of a mass at the apex of the lung. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest CT with contrast. REQUEST TEST: MRI Thoracic Spine to evaluate for cord compression.
